user_feedback: Consistency improved, but overall animations often became less interesting.
assessment: Prior acceptance emphasized anatomy persistence and readable continuity too strongly. Several final compositions lost abundance, natural asymmetry, fine detail or dramatic scale; Brew and Starlit also have extended stretches with little new visual development.
assumed_direction: Use the strongest original compositions as the minimum target, retaining successful repairs and approved concept changes such as the Latte-art heart.
direction_preference: An optional user preference between preserving strong original compositions and more expressive new finishes was requested; the audit itself is independent of that choice.
quality_bar: Approve the mature composition before animation. At148px in both themes and at equal artwork size, it must retain or deliberately improve the original distinctive silhouette, abundance, asymmetry and species/concept landmarks.

Lock the final anatomy inventory and relative proportions: branches, heads/fruit/buds, petal tiers, tendrils, small supporting motifs, and blossom-to-bean scale. Do not reduce that inventory merely to make continuity easier.

Work backward from that final: establish attachment sites early, introduce smaller closed forms on those exact sites, unfold existing surfaces, then complete staggered bloom/ripening. Preserve companion buds/flowers if they make the final composition richer.
Use two independent acceptance gates: final design interest and all24 transition continuity. Passing counts, pixel uniqueness or no-regression tests cannot compensate for a bland endpoint.

Make every final-row pose perform a visible job at148px: last petals release, a second spray opens, a pendant extends, final berries ripen, or luminous detail resolves. Plan these jobs before generation, without deleting final detail to create an easy sequence.

Check both fixed-canvas prominence and equal-occupied-size comparisons. Standard padding explains some shrinkage; larger losses such as Queen of the Night at64% of its old occupied height deserve explicit review. If the hero becomes timid, repair the source coherently instead of using per-frame zoom.

Preserve controlled irregularity: unequal heights, varied orientations, overlap/negative space and different developmental stages. Consistency means stable identity through time, not bilateral symmetry or identical parts.
Repair damaged transparency using painted opaque anatomy. Do not canonize clipped or missing old pixels as desirable texture; restore intended richness, not rendering defects.

signature.evidence: comparison-01..06-fit.png and comparison-01..06-fixed.png; exact F25 crops and source hashes in evidence.json.
signature.conclusion: The feedback is justified. The revision often preserved component identity over time by replacing rich, irregular compositions with smaller inventories of larger, more regular parts. This was not necessary for consistency. Recent berry repairs recover much of their original abundance, but several non-berry endings still materially underperform.
signature.our_review_tradeoff: Earlier reviews over-weighted intact surfaces and stable counts/poses. A valid consistency repair was sometimes accepted even when the target composition itself had been simplified. The final design needs its own explicit interest gate.

boundaries: This task directly inspects all44 mature final compositions, not a new live or full-sequence temporal audit.

27 original assets are read from b7914c30;17 later-added signature/botanical originals are absent there and instead come from archived pre-revision sheets whose hashes match the original44 review evidence. Per-file provenance is explicit.
Fit contacts scale whole copied poses only for visual comparison; fixed contacts retain the original/current256px coordinate frame. Neither modifies artwork or production resources.
Original near-transparent/absent surfaces can look like fine detail; damaged alpha is treated separately from intended compositional richness.
Priority indicates design-restoration value, not a claim that current native rendering is broken.

botanical.scope: 15 botanical animations previously assigned to this reviewer; berries excluded because already redesigned and reviewed separately.
botanical.comparison_boundary: Current production F25 and currentF21-F25 inspected against originalF25 at native256px and opaque148px dark composites. This is a terminal-design audit, not a fresh all25 continuity or live timing audit. Originalb7914c30 was used for12 species; Fuchsia/Magnolia/Iris did not exist there, so40aa87f5 originals were used and all15 original SHA values verified against the prior review.
botanical.main_finding: Consistency was often achieved by reducing the final design's complexity: fewer flower nodes, simpler branches, more symmetric layouts and quieter last rows. A richer locked final should constrain the growth sequence, rather than a conservative growth template deciding the finish.

workflow: Review and approve one genuinely interesting final at148px in light/dark before generating growth. Compare it directly with the original, including subject-to-bean ratio, silhouette, head count, asymmetry and species details.

Fix the exact mature branch graph and node inventory from that final. Persistent nodes do not require mirrored branches, equal flower sizes or all buds to open. A retained side bud can be part of the mature design.

Define 4-6 complete structural key poses backward from the final: mature finish, partially open full branch graph, visible bud groups, formed stems/leaves, small established crown, sprout. Keep the same fixed bean and camera throughout.

Generate complete pose banks with explicit retained anatomy in every state. Early poses can have sparse buds at future head locations; late poses must not delete branches or invent final-frame abundance.

Allocate the last five frames to finishing named existing structures: successive distal hearts, lower raceme tiers, the last snowdrop bell, inner radial rays or a small side head. Avoid five almost-finished repaints, but allow one final settle.

Use overlapping context poses when generating banks and curate only whole native-generated frames. Use one common source scale per coherent bank and a fixed final envelope; do not compensate for poor anatomy with per-frame zoom, component swaps or fabricated transitions.
Run two independent gates: design interest at148px versus original, then continuity of every adjacent pair. Passing counts and hashes cannot establish an interesting finish.
botanical.scale_note: Some originals encroach on cell edges. Do not preserve unsafe clipping or infer that every smaller final is a regression. Rafflesia/Bee Orchid already use the safe envelope; Queen of the Night/Poppy still leave material room unused.

core.scope: Five coffee designs: all 25 original and current frames. All 44 original/current final poses compared at fixed 148px cell scale. Endpoint observations for other designs do not establish their full animation behavior.
core.provenance: Originals use b7914c30 where the path exists. Missing IDs use archived pre-revision RGBA atlases whose SHA256 matches the original review evidence. Per-asset origins and hashes are in evidence.json.
core.verdict: The user feedback is supported. Continuity improved, but several rich endpoint silhouettes were simplified or reduced, while some coffee animations still spend too many frames on the same established motif. The latest heart and fruit follow-ups are useful improvements, so this does not justify another uniform redesign of all 44.
core.why_prior_acceptance_was_insufficient: Our earlier acceptance checks established anatomy persistence, distinct images, stable framing, and an ordered finish. They were too permissive about quiet stretches and did not consistently require the final artwork to match the original richness or the whole sequence to have a compelling visual story. Passing those checks was not proof that the animation became more interesting.
separate_causes: Framing loss: several original finals occupied around 230-250 source pixels while current finals are substantially smaller. Fixed-size comparisons make this visible; tight-crop comparisons would hide it.

Anatomy loss: Bleeding heart, Jade vine, Chocolate cosmos, and Myosotis simplify branching, cluster density, or differentiated foliage. Enlarging these replacements alone cannot restore the lost character.
Narrative loss or stagnation: Brew and Starlit remain larger or similarly sized, yet too many poses repeat the same steam/loop idea. Adding detail or enlarging them would not solve that.

Regularization: many replacements favor equally spaced leaves, front-facing symmetry, thick smooth outlines, and uniform color. Those improve legibility but can erase the natural gesture and layered depth that made the original distinctive.

framing_findings.metric_boundary: Alpha >=24 occupied bounds and area describe footprint, not quality or anatomical detail. F1 height is a bean-size proxy; no semantic bean segmentation was performed. Whole-cell fixed-scale views were used without per-frame fitting.
framing_findings.important_distinction: A bigger bean is not universal. Current F1 beans are smaller for the latest Coffee plant and berry follow-ups. Their height-growth ratios often improve even though the final plant remains smaller. Growth ratio and terminal presence therefore need separate acceptance checks.
framing_findings.core_counterexample: Brew final height grows from 180 to209px, Latte180 to209, Starlit192 to195, and Flower198 to196. Core loss of interest cannot be attributed to a universal reduction in the final footprint.
framing_findings.underfill_caveat: Queen of the night has current final height145px and maximum height148px across all25, far below the approximately208px available height. Bleeding heart final171px/max177px is similarly underfilled. A global padding cap alone is not a sufficient explanation; source composition and common bank scaling also require inspection.

core_designs.preserve: Clear golden warmth, split-bean origin, and larger readable terminal footprint.
core_designs.diagnosis: The current central steam stroke and two side curls are effectively established by F10. F11-25 mostly increase thickness, width, or brightness. The original also had this weakness, so consistency repaired a weak concept without making it substantially more engaging. The original fine secondary filaments and small glints made the terminal feel more airy; current thick smooth tubes are bolder but closer to a fixed flame emblem.
core_designs.smallest_direction: Keep a recognizably warm aromatic finish, but design three readable stages: pressure gathering at the split, one rising ribbon that branches into unequal returning curls, and a final broad layered plume. Let the curl tips travel and the central ribbon unfurl across the last row instead of scaling an already complete trident. Preserve negative space and a few fine internal filaments at the final size.
frame_focus: F1-3 are nearly the same closed bean.
F6-8 repeat the established rising ribbon.
F10-25 reuse the complete three-armed motif; this is the major interest deficit.

core_designs.priority: High: separate its story from Brew
core_designs.preserve: The three luminous loops and five outer stars remain legible; terminal size and inventory are not materially reduced.
core_designs.diagnosis: It borrows almost the whole Brew grammar: split bean, vertical flame, side curls, then a late third loop. The thick soft glow reduces the original fine double-line delicacy. F6-8, F13-15, F16-18, and much of F21-25 are quiet groups, so stars feel appended to a steam symbol rather than the reason for the transformation.
core_designs.smallest_direction: Make starlight the causal action: one spark rises along a curved path, the path loops back into the first petal, then two more luminous arcs close at distinct times. Outer stars should appear as the traveling tip reaches their positions. Reserve the center light and final upper arc closure for the finish. Keep all established arcs and stars; do not use random spark flicker as substitute motion.
frame_focus: F5-18 remains visually close to Brew.

core_designs.priority: Targeted pacing refinement; not a lost-richness rebuild
core_designs.preserve: Five ivory petals, golden stamens, clean final anatomy, and near-original terminal height. Current flower is actually wider and has slightly greater occupied area.
core_designs.diagnosis: This is not evidence of petal-count loss. The simple terminal was already simple. The large persistent bean limits total height growth: current F1 bean128px versus final196px. The central bud holds around F10-13; later petals broaden through F16-22 before the lower/front pair becomes clear in F23-25. The staged opening is coherent but mechanically symmetrical.
core_designs.smallest_direction: Keep the accepted final flower. Give the bud a visible seam and slight directional lean, open rear and side petals on staggered beats, and let the front pair unfurl with visible curvature earlier in the last third. If more terminal impact is desired, approve a proportion study with a smaller constant bean and more stem/flower space before rebuilding the atlas.
frame_focus: F1-3 and F10-13 are the quietest sections.
F16-22 could carry clearer petal curvature changes.
F23-25 provides a real front-petal finish and should be preserved.

core_designs.priority: Preserve heart direction; optional middle refinement
core_designs.preserve: The heart is the clearest improved identity in the coffee set: broad warm ivory surface, recognizable cleft and point, larger terminal presence, useful visible final-row shaping. The user explicitly selected the heart.
core_designs.diagnosis: The original rosetta had more internal repeated lobes but a long finished hold. The new heart is an intentional simplification with a stronger readable destination, not an accidental loss of plant anatomy. Its weakness is F9-14: a horizontal oval simply widens. F15-20 then gradually indents the same pillow before the taller heart finishes.
core_designs.smallest_direction: Keep the selected final heart and its warm milk material. If revisited, carry a visible flowing fold through the oval phase so the two lobes arise from the ribbon; pull the central stroke down later into the point. Improve the journey without returning to a generic cream plant or inventing more decorative complexity.
frame_focus: F2-8 is a distinct fluid beginning.
F9-14 is the least purposeful middle.
F21-25 shows meaningful cleft, point, and lobe development.

core_designs.priority: Preserve richer payoff; optional natural-gesture refinement
core_designs.preserve: Four red cherries, glossy recognizably coffee-like leaves, broad terminal width, and ordered late ripening. The original b7914c30 final has leaves but no cherries, so the latest design adds a genuine narrative destination.
core_designs.diagnosis: The current plant is richer but looks like three tidy horizontal leaf tiers with evenly paired cherries. It loses some spontaneous stem gesture, though it does not lose the original fruit inventory. The bean is smaller, not larger: F1 height75px versus original123px. Final height falls197 to177px but width grows177 to200px; the result is a squat broad shrub with a stronger relative growth ratio.
core_designs.smallest_direction: Keep all four persistent fruit nodes and the late green-to-yellow-to-red progression. If refining, offset branch heights slightly, vary leaf angles, and retain a little woody stem between tiers. Judge a final silhouette with more vertical reach before expanding it into25 states; avoid another perfectly mirrored branch ladder.
frame_focus: F6-8 and F11-13 mostly enlarge settled leaf pairs.
F14-18 establishes and enlarges fruit nodes.

set_endpoint_priorities.reason: Largest combined loss of footprint, asymmetrical architecture, and distinctive abundance. Queen loses the dramatic broad side bloom and tall cactus presence; Bleeding heart loses the long multi-branch hanging arrangement; Jade vine loses the dense cascading raceme and curling woody structure.
Several branching flower heads become a tidy few, and delicate differentiated foliage becomes generic broad leaves. This is a design simplification even when occupied area alone stays similar.

Review final framing and characteristic silhouette before requesting more detail. Rafflesia is smaller but retains five fleshy lobes; Passionflower loses some overall dramatic reach; the poppy is markedly smaller; Bird of paradise is shorter and more compact.
Final scale is adequate, but the full25-frame journeys need more distinct visual events and less shared flame/loop choreography.

positive_controls: Latte heart: clear species-independent visual identity and a real shaped finish.
Coffee plant: cherries add a meaningful final event beyond leaf expansion.
Rose and Sunflower: bolder readable mature flower heads without an obvious endpoint inventory collapse.
Recent berry follow-ups: restored persistent fruit and flower counts; retain these fixes while assessing final footprint separately.
final_first_quality_bar: First approve F25 beside the exact old F25 at the same whole-cell display size in both themes. Do not independently fit or zoom the candidates. Ask whether the new endpoint is at least as desirable and distinctive, not merely cleaner.

Record characteristic architecture, mature flower/fruit inventory, negative spaces, asymmetry, palette, and surface texture. Preserve those intentional features unless the redesign explicitly changes the concept, as with the chosen latte heart.

Set terminal occupied bounds and bean-to-canopy proportions from that approved art. Retain transparent safety space, but do not impose a uniform visual shrink on every species. Inspect unusually underfilled assets before blaming padding alone.

Approve five or six meaningful key poses backward from the finish. They should describe visibly different stages without needing labels: emergence, structure, formation, unfolding or ripening, and completion.

Fill the25 poses around those milestones with persistent anatomy. A low pixel-difference or high pixel-difference score cannot replace judging whether a transition contributes visible form, motion, or intentional anticipation.

Review the entire sequence at148px plus a fixed-speed offline playback, then native paused captures. Judge terminal appeal, narrative interest, and technical continuity independently; passing one must not compensate for failing another.

Keep a controlled number of small asymmetries and overlaps from the final target. Consistency should mean the same living object persists, not that every leaf and petal becomes evenly spaced or perfectly mirrored.
core.recommendation: Do not automatically regenerate all44. First separate source-framing fixes from anatomy restoration, then redesign the two weak coffee stories. Retain successful heart/fruit work. Require endpoint and milestone approval before spending another25-frame generation on each priority.
core.boundary: Read-only artwork audit with QA-only analytical contacts and notes. No image generation, production changes, Git mutations, device actions, live playback, or runtime timing validation.

original_and_current_provenance.method: Exact row-major F25 256px RGBA crops, whole-cell resize to148px, opaque analytical composites; no fitting or artwork editing, no runtime translation/halo.

footprint_metrics.method: Alpha >=24 occupied bounds/area on exact source RGBA. F1 height is an initial-bean proxy, bottom32 width a base-width proxy, not semantic bean segmentation. Translation does not affect dimensions. Raw area does not establish detail or quality.

validation_boundary: Static original/current final comparisons at fixed148px and equal occupied size, plus botanical final-row reviews and all25 poses of the five coffee designs. This reassessment is not a fresh all44 full-transition review or live Android playback test. Footprint measurements describe size, not perceptual quality; old damaged alpha is not treated as desirable detail.
